tour.name: Italy Highlights 8-Day Private Tour: Rome, Florence, Tuscany & Venice
tour.subtitle: Eight days through the classic Italy with licensed guides in every city: the Colosseum and the Vatican in Rome, Michelangelo's David and the Uffizi in Florence, Siena and the Chianti vineyards, and St Mark's and a gondola in Venice, with first-class high-speed trains and seven nights in central hotels.

tour.metaDescription: 8-day private Italy tour: Rome's Colosseum, Forum and Vatican, Florence's David and Uffizi, Siena, San Gimignano and Chianti, Venice's St Mark's, Doge's Palace and gondola. Guides, high-speed trains, 7 nights with breakfast.

tour.overview:
Rome, Florence and Venice are the three cities most travellers dream of when they think of Italy, and each tells a different chapter of the story: the empire and the popes in Rome, the Renaissance in Florence, and the trading republic on the water in Venice. Between Florence and the south lie the hills of Tuscany, with their medieval towns and vineyards. All four are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

This private journey links them with first-class high-speed trains, which run city centre to city centre in under two hours and spare you the motorways and the parking. You have a licensed guide in every city, a private car for the Tuscan countryside, timed tickets for every major museum and seven nights in well-located hotels within walking distance of the sights. The guided visits are in the mornings and early afternoons, leaving the evenings free for dinners, piazzas and gelato.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 8 days, 7 nights
• Start: Rome Fiumicino Airport or your hotel in Rome
• End: Venice Marco Polo Airport, Venice station or your hotel
• Type: private tour with licensed guides, private cars and drivers, high-speed trains; 7 nights in hotels with breakfast
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, hotels, trains, museum slots and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; daily walks of 4 to 7 km

WHAT YOU SEE
• Rome: the Colosseum, the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, the Pantheon, Piazza Navona and the Trevi Fountain.
• Vatican City: the Vatican Museums, the Sistine Chapel and St Peter's Basilica.
• Florence: Michelangelo's David, the Duomo, the Uffizi and the Ponte Vecchio.
• Tuscany: Siena, a Chianti wine estate and San Gimignano.
• Venice: St Mark's Basilica, the Doge's Palace, the Rialto and a gondola ride.

WHY THIS WORKS
Three nights in Rome and three in Florence avoid packing every other day, and the trains take less time than the drive to the airport would. Every museum is booked at a quiet time, so you see more and queue less.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Italy, couples, honeymooners, families and small groups who want the great classics with private guiding.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want the coast, ask us to add two nights in Sorrento or on the Amalfi Coast with our Pompeii and Amalfi days. If you prefer one base, choose our day tours.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Vatican, Accademia and Uffizi tickets are personal: we need each traveller's full name when you book. The Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays and the Florentine museums on Mondays; we arrange the days around your dates. Italy has a city tax per person per night, paid at the hotels.

days.name: Arrival in Rome and an evening walk to the Trevi Fountain
days.description:
What to expect: a private welcome at the airport and a gentle first evening in the Eternal City.

Your driver meets you in the arrivals hall at Rome Fiumicino with a name sign and drives you to your hotel in the historic centre, about 45 minutes away. After time to rest, your guide meets you in the late afternoon for a short walk to the Trevi Fountain, where you throw the coin that promises a return to Rome, the Spanish Steps and the Pantheon square at dusk, with tips for dinner in the lanes around.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
Any time – Private transfer from the airport to your hotel.
17:30 – Evening orientation walk: Trevi Fountain, Spanish Steps, Pantheon square.

GOOD TO KNOW
• If you arrive late, the evening walk moves to another day.

INCLUDED: airport transfer, evening walk with a licensed guide.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Rome.
Meals: none.

days.name: Ancient Rome: Colosseum, Roman Forum, Palatine Hill and Piazza Navona
days.description:
What to expect: the heart of the Roman Empire with a licensed guide and timed tickets.

You start at the Colosseum at opening time, before the heat and the crowds. Your guide explains how the amphitheatre, opened in the year 80, held 50,000 spectators and how the games were staged from the underground passages. You walk under the Arch of Titus into the Roman Forum, along the Via Sacra past the Temple of Vesta and the Senate House, and climb the Palatine Hill, where the emperors lived above the Circus Maximus. After a Roman lunch – cacio e pepe or carbonara – you see the Pantheon's great dome from inside and Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers in Piazza Navona. The rest of the afternoon is free.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Colosseum (about 1 hour 15 minutes).
10:30 – Roman Forum and Palatine Hill.
13:00 – Lunch in a trattoria.
14:30 – Pantheon and Piazza Navona.
15:30 – Free afternoon.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Large bags and backpacks are not allowed in the Colosseum.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, Colosseum, Forum, Palatine and Pantheon tickets, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Rome.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Vatican City: Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel and St Peter's Basilica
days.description:
What to expect: the treasures of the popes with an early timed entry and a licensed guide.

You enter the Vatican Museums among the first visitors of the day. Your guide leads you through the ancient sculptures of the Pio-Clementino, the Gallery of Maps and Raphael's Rooms, with the School of Athens, to the Sistine Chapel, where Michelangelo painted the ceiling between 1508 and 1512 and the Last Judgment from 1536 to 1541. You continue into St Peter's Basilica to see Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's bronze canopy under the great dome, then step out into St Peter's Square. After lunch in the Prati district, the afternoon is free: many travellers climb the dome or explore Trastevere.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Vatican Museums and Raphael Rooms.
10:30 – Sistine Chapel.
11:15 – St Peter's Basilica and Square.
13:00 – Lunch in Prati.
14:30 – Free afternoon.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Shoulders and knees must be covered.
• On a Sunday we swap this day with day 2.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel tickets, guided basilica visit, lunch, transfers.
NOT INCLUDED: dome climb, dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Rome.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: High-speed train to Florence: the Duomo, Piazza della Signoria and Ponte Vecchio
days.description:
What to expect: a fast train through the Italian countryside and a first walk through Renaissance Florence.

After breakfast, your driver takes you to Roma Termini for a first-class high-speed train to Florence, about 1 hour 35 minutes. Your guide meets you at Santa Maria Novella station and, after you drop your bags at the hotel and have lunch, leads you to the Piazza del Duomo, with Brunelleschi's dome, built between 1420 and 1436, Giotto's bell tower and the Baptistery's golden Gates of Paradise. You continue through the medieval streets to Piazza della Signoria and the Palazzo Vecchio, and end on the Ponte Vecchio, the bridge of the goldsmiths. The evening is free.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:30 – Transfer to Roma Termini.
10:30 – High-speed train to Florence.
12:15 – Hotel and lunch.
14:30 – Duomo, Baptistery, Piazza della Signoria and Ponte Vecchio.
17:00 – Free evening.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Luggage travels with you on the train; there is space at the end of each carriage.

INCLUDED: transfers, first-class train, licensed guide, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dome climb, dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Florence.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Florence: Michelangelo's David, the Uffizi and Piazzale Michelangelo
days.description:
What to expect: the greatest art of the Renaissance, with timed tickets and a licensed guide.

You see Michelangelo's David at the Accademia at opening time, the 5.17-metre marble giant carved between 1501 and 1504, and his unfinished Prisoners struggling out of the stone. After lunch near the Central Market, your guide leads you through the Uffizi: Giotto, Botticelli's Birth of Venus and Primavera, Leonardo da Vinci's Annunciation, Michelangelo, Raphael and Caravaggio. At the end of the afternoon, a car takes you up to Piazzale Michelangelo for the view over the whole city.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Accademia Gallery.
10:00 – Central Market and the San Lorenzo district.
12:30 – Lunch.
14:00 – Uffizi Gallery (about 2 hours).
16:30 – Piazzale Michelangelo by car.
17:15 – Free evening.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Accademia and the Uffizi are closed on Mondays; on a Monday we swap this day with day 6.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, Accademia and Uffizi tickets, lunch, car to Piazzale Michelangelo.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Florence.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Tuscany: Siena, lunch at a Chianti wine estate and San Gimignano
days.description:
What to expect: the Tuscan hills and two medieval towns, with a private car, a licensed guide and a winery lunch.

Your driver and guide collect you at your hotel and drive south to Siena. You walk to the Piazza del Campo, the shell-shaped square where the Palio horse race is run on 2 July and 16 August, and visit the striped marble cathedral, with its inlaid floor and the frescoed Piccolomini Library. You then drive into the Chianti hills along cypress-lined roads to a family wine estate for a vineyard walk, a Tuscan lunch and a tasting of Chianti Classico and olive oil. In the afternoon you explore San Gimignano and its 14 medieval towers, with time for a famous gelato, before driving back to Florence.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)

09:15 – Siena: Piazza del Campo and the cathedral.
12:30 – Drive into Chianti.
13:00 – Vineyard walk, lunch and wine tasting.

17:15 – Drive back to Florence.
18:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Non-alcoholic drinks are always available at the tasting.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Siena Cathedral ticket, winery lunch and tasting.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Florence.

days.name: High-speed train to Venice: the Doge's Palace, St Mark's Basilica, Rialto and a gondola
days.description:
What to expect: the city on the water in one full afternoon, with a licensed guide, reserved tickets and a private gondola.

After an early breakfast, your driver takes you to the station for a first-class high-speed train to Venice, about 2 hours 15 minutes, arriving at Santa Lucia station right on the Grand Canal. Your guide meets you and a water taxi takes you along the Grand Canal to your hotel. After lunch of cicchetti in a traditional bacaro, you visit the Doge's Palace, cross the Bridge of Sighs into the old prisons, and enter St Mark's Basilica, whose domes are covered with golden mosaics. You walk through quiet canals to the Rialto Bridge and end the day with a private gondola ride.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:15 – Transfer to Firenze Santa Maria Novella.
09:00 – High-speed train to Venice.
11:15 – Water taxi along the Grand Canal to your hotel.
12:30 – Cicchetti lunch.
14:00 – Doge's Palace and Bridge of Sighs.
15:45 – St Mark's Basilica.
16:45 – Rialto Bridge and gondola ride.
17:45 – Free evening.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Large backpacks are not allowed in St Mark's Basilica.
• As hotel guests, you are exempt from the Venice day-visitor access fee.

INCLUDED: transfers, first-class train, water taxi, licensed guide, Doge's Palace and basilica tickets, gondola, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Venice.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Departure from Venice
days.description:
What to expect: a last morning in Venice and a private transfer by water.

After breakfast, you have free time for a last walk, the Rialto market or a visit to the island of Murano to watch glassblowers, which we can arrange. At the time that suits your flight or train, a private water taxi takes you across the lagoon to Venice Marco Polo Airport, or to the station.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
Morning – Free time.
As needed – Private water taxi to the airport or station.

GOOD TO KNOW
• We can add extra nights in Venice or a boat day to Murano and Burano.

INCLUDED: private water taxi transfer.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, hotels, trains, museum slots and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are the trains and museum tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: first-class high-speed trains Rome–Florence and Florence–Venice, and timed tickets for the Colosseum, Vatican Museums, Accademia, Uffizi, Siena Cathedral, Doge's Palace and St Mark's Basilica.

faq.question: What kind of hotels are used?
faq.answer: Comfortable 4-star or boutique hotels in the historic centres, within walking distance of the main sights. Upgrades to 5-star hotels are available on request.

faq.question: Is the city tax included?
faq.answer: No. Italian cities charge a small tax per person per night, paid directly at each hotel. We tell you the amounts when we confirm.

faq.question: Will we have the same guide throughout?
faq.answer: You have a licensed local guide in each city, because Italian guiding licences are regional and local guides know their cities best.

faq.question: Can we add the Amalfi Coast or Cinque Terre?
faq.answer: Yes. We often add two nights in Sorrento for Pompeii and the Amalfi Coast after Rome, or a day in Cinque Terre from Florence.

faq.question: Can we do the route in reverse?
faq.answer: Yes. The tour can start in Venice and end in Rome, or be adapted to your flights.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the Colosseum, the gondola and the gelato. We can book family rooms and shorten museum visits.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The trains and most museums are accessible, but Venice has many bridges with steps and some old-town streets are uneven. Tell us your needs and we will adapt.

faq.question: How much walking is there?
faq.answer: About 4 to 7 km a day at an easy pace, with cars, trains and boats for the longer distances.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, sun protection in summer, and clothes covering shoulders and knees for the Vatican, St Mark's and the cathedrals.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October. July and August are hot and busy; November to March is quieter, with shorter days and lower hotel prices.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 21 days before the tour starts; museum and train tickets may not be refundable after purchase. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
